desc:
A binary tree can be written down by a preorder walk that also records the empty spots: write the node's value, then the serialization of its left child, then the serialization of its right child, and write -1 in place of every missing child. So a single node 7 is [7, -1, -1], and the empty tree is [-1]. Real node values are non-negative.

Given an integer array seq, decide whether it is the serialization of some binary tree. It must describe one complete tree: nothing may be missing at the end and nothing may be left over. The empty array is not a valid serialization.

For example [5, 1, -1, -1, 7, -1, -1] is valid (root 5 with children 1 and 7), [5, 1, -1, -1, 7, -1] is not (the right child of 7 is missing), and [-1, 5, -1, -1] is not (the first -1 already completes the tree).

Do not rebuild the tree; a single pass with O(1) extra memory is enough.
constraints: -1 stands for a missing child, every other value is a real node
hints: Think about how many entries the rest of the array still has to supply while you read it from left to right.
Keep a counter of “open slots”. At the beginning exactly one slot is open: the root. Reading an element fills one slot.
A real node fills one slot and opens two new ones (its children); a -1 only fills a slot. If you ever need a slot while none is open, the answer is false; at the end exactly zero slots must remain.
editorial: Count the open slots. Initially there is one: the place for the root. Every element of the array must go into an open slot, otherwise the sequence has extra data (return false as soon as you meet an element while the count is zero). A value other than -1 is a real node: it uses up one slot and creates two new ones, one for each child, so the net change is +1. A -1 only consumes a slot, net change -1.

After the last element, the serialization is complete exactly when no slot is left open. A short array leaves slots open, a long one runs out of slots early. This is a single left-to-right scan, O(n) time and O(1) space; the preorder structure guarantees that the order in which slots are filled does not matter for the count. The empty array fails because the root slot stays open.
